styleAnswer.evidence: The anvil is a small, thin grey object, less than one tile, with only 11 distinct colours. It has roughly 3 visible grey steps: a light top face, a mid body and a dark base. It does not have the per-surface highlights or grain of the references. 76% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline reads as a neutral dark line, close to the sticker look. The well, stall and hedge references carry 9-20 visible tones per tile and tinted edges (0-33% neutral), and the candidate is clearly flatter and thinner than these. The object is small, so the per-tile density fact is not used against it. By eye, the metal has no stepped shading, no specular glints, no surface pitting and no material-toned edge, so a careful artist would not accept it beside the references. The anvil's shape is recognisable and cleanly drawn, but that is not enough to pass.
